fixes.explanation: That's right, friend. David says, "In God alone my soul finds rest…" There's no "and my own strength" tacked on the end. His rest comes from God, and so does his salvation. I tried resting on my own strength once, and I'm telling you, my mustache gave out before I did.

I see why you'd go there, with a fortress in the picture. But David doesn't say a word about battles in this verse. He says, "I will never be shaken." That's his confidence, and it rests on who God is, not on a win-loss record.

Yes, baker. David says, "They fully intend to cast him down from his lofty perch…" Fully intend! They didn't wander into it, they came with a whole plan. And still David tells his soul to rest in God (Psalm 62:5).
You got it, baker. David says, "God has spoken once; I have heard this twice: that power belongs to God…" Whatever else is loud in the world, the power is God's. That's the line to hold onto.

I understand the guess, since David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), baker. But the verse says he heard "that power belongs to God…" Nothing about his kingdom lasting. The power is God's, and that's the whole point.
That's right, baker. David says, "For You will repay each man according to his deeds." Not by bank account, not by family name. It's what a person has done. That's how David closes the psalm.

Good guess, since David mentioned the lowborn, baker. But the verse says, "…You will repay each man according to his deeds." Whether a person is lowborn or exalted isn't what he names here. Deeds are the word.
